newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Gencor to decide on zinc smelter next year.
newsitem.headline: Gencor to decide on zinc smelter next year.

text.p: Gencor Ltd will decide next year whether to go ahead with the construction of a 1.7 billion rand zinc smelter in South Africa's Eastern Cape Province, a company official said.
Gencor zinc project director John Taylor told Reuters a feasibility study into the smelter about 50 percent complete.
"We are about halfway through the feasibility which should finish round about February/March next year.

"Assuming it still looks good at that stage, (we will) go for approval through the Gencor exco (executive committee) and board. If that is approved then we start construction next year with the idea of being in production in late 1999," Taylor said.
Gencor was looking at sites near East London and Port Elizabeth for the smelter, which would have a design capacity of 220,000 tonnes of zinc produced from mostly imported concentrates.
The plant would have the capacity for expansion to around 400,000 tonnes -- which could possibly make it the largest zinc smelter in the world.
"The whole layout is put together with the idea that the plant could be doubled. It will make it the biggest (in the world)," Taylor said.
The zinc produced would be exported mainly to the Far East, and at current zinc prices it could pull in more than a billion rand in foreign exchange earnings for South Africa.
"We are looking at either Port Elizabeth or East London, there is a third possibility if a new port should be developed in the vicinity of the Kouga river," Taylor said.

Analysts said the Eastern Cape, one of South Africa's poorest areas with some of the country's highest unemployment figures, would be an ideal area to erect the smelter, which could create hundreds of new jobs.
The smelter could import around 440,000 tonnes of zinc concentrates a year from, among others, Australia, Alaska and Peru.
And it would also produce a number of by-products, most importantly sulphuric acid.
Other by-products which could be produced are copper, cadmium, nickel, mercury, germanium, lead, cobalt and silver.
